openai.feedback:
Yes—the durability fix should exist, but the reviewer-return gap needs a code-level fallback rather than a prose-only instruction.

The smallest thing that would do — extend the existing mini-plan and `reviews.json` mechanisms as proposed, and add a narrowly scoped `SubagentStop` salvage hook that writes an unrecorded reviewer reply to the existing payload/record path.

What it costs to keep — ownership of hook lifecycle, run-id resolution, transcript-format compatibility, and ensuring the fallback remains subordinate to the normal orchestrator record path.

What it forecloses — changing reviewer transcript/output conventions without updating the salvage hook.

Category: ownership
Severity: medium
Finding: The immediate-write rule depends on an orchestrator remembering to act before compaction; it is an ongoing human-discipline obligation and does not make reviewer findings durable in the failure mode this change is meant to address.
Suggestion: Build the named, narrowly scoped `SubagentStop` salvage fallback now, reusing the repository’s existing run-id-resolution approach and writing only when the normal review payload has not already been recorded.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
